summary: The Earth Analog: A Stickman's Guide to Surviving Space is an interactive, story driven UI/UX prototype that transforms complex space science into an accessible visual survival guide. Before launching expensive hardware or astronauts to the Moon and Mars, space agencies test equipment in extreme environments on Earth known as planetary analogs. Using original hand-drawn stickman illustrations and clickable navigation, this project explores two extreme terrestrial analog sites based on NASA space exploration resources: Svalbard (Arctic) for freezing lunar South Pole conditions, and Kawah Ijen (Indonesia) for hyper acidic Martian environments and Planetary Protection. By combining humor, visual storytelling, and official NASA mission resources, the project helps students and general audiences understand how Earth-based analog research keeps off world exploration safe.
details:
How It Works:

The Earth Analog is an interactive UI/UX educational prototype designed with clickable mission navigation. Users follow a stickman explorer across two extreme terrestrial analog phases before heading to space:

1. Phase 1 – Deep Freeze Simulation (Svalbard, Arctic): Simulates extreme sub-zero lunar South Pole conditions to illustrate how space engineers test spacesuit flexibility, battery survival, and rover mobility.

2. Phase 2 – Corrosive Environment & Planetary Protection (Kawah Ijen, Indonesia): Uses East Java's hyper-acidic crater lake (pH -0.5) as a terrestrial analog for harsh Martian environments to demonstrate material durability testing and chemical sterilization protocols for Planetary Protection.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

This project bridges intimidating aerospace engineering concepts with relatable visual storytelling for students, educators, and the general public. By highlighting Kawah Ijen in Indonesia as a scientifically valuable planetary analog, it also fosters local STEM pride and demonstrates how Earth-based field research protects both astronauts and off world ecosystems.

Tools, Software & Creativity:

Developed solo without code using original hand-drawn stickman illustrations, Canva for interactive UI/UX prototyping and slide layout, Google Docs for documentation, and official NASA imagery and space exploration resources. Key design considerations included mobile readability, zero code accessibility, and translating technical spaceflight concepts into clear visual narratives.
